vignetting.model: DERIVED: the design aperture (EXPP Table 1: x from -397 to +303 ft, y = +-388 ft, ellipse about x0 = -47 ft) is mapped onto the sphere (radius 870 ft, GUIDE) for a beam at zenith angle za; an aperture point (x, y) reflects at C - sqrt(R^2 - x^2 - y^2) s + x e_x + y e_y and lies on the dish if its angle from the downward vertical is <= the rim half-angle asin(500/870). gain_factor = (sum of field on dish / sum of field)^2 with field = sqrt(EXPP power illumination, -7 dB edge, rolloff 6), feed power fixed.
vignetting.onset_basis: DERIVED: uphill edge x = +303 ft reaches the rim when za = asin(500/870) - asin(303/870) = 35.080 - 20.382
vignetting.compare: EXPP design: "about 1.0 dB" loss at maximum za; EXPP Table 2 1400 MHz 11 -> 9 K/Jy from ZA 15 to 20 = -0.87 dB (DERIVED); this simple model gives -0.67 dB at 19.7 deg.

illuminated.name: illum_orientation
illuminated.value: smaller (700 ft = 213 m) along the uphill-downhill (zenith-angle) direction, larger (776 ft = 237 m) transverse (azimuth direction)
illuminated.quote: The aperture in this design is elliptical, being larger in the transverse dimension than in the uphill-downhill direction.

alt.quote: x is positive towards increasing zenith angle
1) uphill dimension x = +303 ft ... 2) downhill dimension x = -397 ft ... 3) transverse dimension y = 388 ft
Arecibo’s beam is elliptical by design; φbeam should be 90◦, meaning that the za beam is larger than the az beam.
The major axis of the ellipse is linked to the azimuth of the receiver, so its orientation on the sky changes with telescope configuration.

illuminated.note: Mapping 213 m to the za direction and 237 m to the azimuth direction follows EXPP (x = increasing za; 303 + 397 = 700 ft along x, 2 x 388 = 776 ft along y). On the meridian the za direction is north-south, so ns_m = 213, ew_m = 237 at transit (INFERRED from the geometry; no source states ns/ew).

alt.quote: The gregorian optics is designed for a 700 x 776 feet (213 x 237 meters) illumination. The geometrical mean of this is 225 meters.

alt.quote: choose an aperture illumination which is nearly uniform over much of the area and then rolls off sharply near the edge

illuminated.name: illum_vs_za
illuminated.value: different parts of the spherical primary are illuminated as the feed moves; at high za the illumination spills over the uphill rim onto the ground screen
illuminated.quote: Different sections of the spherical reflector are illuminated, however, depending on the source position. In order to minimize beam distortions and gain variations caused when the illuminated pattern spills over the edges of the primary surface, we constrained most of the observations to moderate zenith angles, less than 17◦

alt.quote: One of the major requirements is the reduction of vignetting at high zenith angles to keep the sensitivity high and the system temperature low. The feed design is offset so the aperture is larger downhill of the paraxial ray, moving the illumination away from the uphill edge of the primary.
At maximum zenith angle, the sensitivity will be reduced about 1.0 dB by vignetting.
At high zenith angles, vignetting over the edge of the primary would be a contributor, but the ground screen shields almost all of the spillover energy from the ground.

beam_relation.value: hpbw = K lambda / D, K = 1.02 (uniform), D = 213 x 237 m optics; geometric mean 225 m
beam_relation.quote: hpbw=K * lambda/Diameter ... For uniform illumination on a spherical dish K=1.02.

alt.quote: The hpbw is converted to diameter using diam=1.02*lambda/hpbw (1.02 is the constant for uniform illumination).
The value plotted is the average hpbw (the average of the major and minor axis). The zenith angle has been limited to 5 < za < 14 degrees.
Arecibo’s theoretical gain, without blockage, is KperJy ≈ 11, which is equivalent to a uniformly illuminated circular aperture with radius 94 m.

status.name: collapse
status.quote: The instrument platform of the 305-meter telescope at Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico fell at approximately 7:55 a.m. Atlantic Standard Time Dec. 1, resulting in damage to the dish and surrounding facilities.

alt.quote: Arecibo Observatory’s 305-meter telescope suffers collapse
December 1, 2020

Initial findings indicate that the top section of all three of the 305-meter telescope’s support towers broke off. As the 900-ton instrument platform fell, the telescope’s support cables also dropped.
